blocks.text: iOS 9 combined proactive search and Siri behavior with new iPad multitasking, transit-aware Maps, redesigned Notes, the first News app, richer Mail tools, and an optional iCloud Drive app.

citations.locator: iOS 9 — Intelligence, New iPad Features, and Built-in Apps

blocks.text: The release also introduced Low Power Mode, smaller update downloads, Metal-backed interface performance, stronger account and passcode defaults, and a broad security repair set spanning payments, networking, the kernel, Safari, and WebKit.
iOS 9.0.1 was a focused maintenance update for devices that could not finish Setup Assistant and for alarms or timers that sometimes failed to sound.
Apple also corrected distorted paused video frames in Safari and Photos and restored cellular data for some devices using a profile-supplied custom APN.

citations.locator: iOS 9.0.1 — paused video and custom APN fixes

blocks.text: iOS 9.0.2 repaired cellular-data settings, iMessage activation, manual iCloud Backup, notification rotation, and Podcasts stability.
Its dedicated security bulletin also documents a lock-screen restriction fix that prevented physical access to photos and contacts through the affected path.
iOS 9.1 refined Live Photos so raising or lowering the phone was excluded from a recording and expanded the emoji keyboard with more than 150 Unicode 7.0 and 8.0 characters.
The release also addressed stability, multitasking performance, Calendar, Game Center, Mail, Messages, carrier activation, App Store updates, and a substantial set of published security defects.
iOS 9.2 expanded Apple Music library workflows, added News Top Stories in three countries, brought Mail Drop to Mail, extended iBooks, and enabled iPhone photo imports through the USB Camera Adapter.

citations.locator: iOS 9.2 — Apple Music, News, Mail, iBooks, and USB Camera Adapter

blocks.text: The update also delivered broad app, keyboard, backup, accessibility, and language corrections, while its security bulletin covered access-control, sandbox, web, media, and system components.
iOS 9.2.1 was a maintenance release whose sole itemized consumer fix allowed an app installation managed by an MDM server to complete.
Apple separately documented security repairs across disk-image parsing, kernel-facing components, WebKit, visited-link privacy, and captive-portal cookie isolation.

iOS 9.3 introduced Night Shift and expanded Notes privacy, News discovery, Health and Activity integration, Apple Music, Photos, iBooks, education deployment, CarPlay, Maps, Wallet, and language support.

The release paired those additions with extensive enterprise, accessibility, backup, activation, battery, Phone, and Mail repairs, plus published security corrections for USB, fonts, networking, the kernel, Messages, profiles, certificates, WebKit, and Wi-Fi.

citations.locator: iOS 9.3 — bug fixes, performance, and stability

blocks.text: iOS 9.3.1 was a narrowly scoped maintenance release that corrected apps becoming unresponsive after a user opened links in Safari or other apps.
Apple’s release-specific security page identifies no new security delta and instead says that iOS 9.3.1 includes the security content of iOS 9.3.

citations.locator: iOS 9.3.1 includes the security content of iOS 9.3

blocks.text: iOS 9.3.2 corrected Bluetooth audio on iPhone SE, dictionary lookups, Japanese Kana email-address entry, VoiceOver’s Alex voice, and MDM installation of Custom B2B apps.
Its security bulletin documents additional privacy, networking, cryptography, kernel, browser-history, lock-screen Siri, and WebKit repairs.
Apple’s consumer notes describe iOS 9.3.3 only as a bug-fix and security update, without assigning names to its general reliability changes.

The dedicated security bulletin is substantially more specific, documenting corrections involving Calendar invitations, stored proxy credentials, relayed FaceTime calls, private Siri contact data, media parsing, the kernel, and WebKit.
iOS 9.3.5 was an explicitly security-focused maintenance release rather than a feature update.

Apple’s bulletin enumerates exactly three corrections: a kernel information disclosure, a kernel memory-corruption path to privileged code execution, and a WebKit memory-corruption path triggered by malicious web content.

citations.locator: Kernel and WebKit — CVE-2016-4655, CVE-2016-4656, and CVE-2016-4657

events.summary: The public iOS 9 release introduced proactive intelligence, iPad multitasking, major built-in app redesigns, power and performance improvements, and a broad security update.

changes.title: Proactive intelligence, Siri, and Spotlight
changes.canonicalSummary: Search and Siri gained contextual suggestions, richer direct answers, photo search, on-screen reminders, transit requests, and contact actions.
changes.summary: iOS began surfacing context-aware information before typing, expanded Spotlight answers and contact actions, and let Siri search personal media, set reminders from visible content, and request transit directions.

changes.title: iPad multitasking
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported iPads gained Slide Over, Split View, and Picture in Picture workflows.
changes.summary: The iPad experience added a temporary second-app panel, side-by-side interaction on supported hardware, and a floating video window that remained visible while using other apps.

changes.title: Expanded iPad QuickType tools
changes.canonicalSummary: The iPad keyboard added text-selection gestures, a Shortcut Bar, and hardware-keyboard shortcuts.
changes.summary: QuickType on iPad introduced multitouch cursor selection, faster access to editing tools, and application shortcuts for connected keyboards.

changes.title: Maps transit and nearby discovery
changes.canonicalSummary: Maps added transit routes, station detail, schedules, nearby-category browsing, and richer place cards in supported locations.
changes.summary: Maps could plan public-transport trips in selected cities, expose station entrances and schedules, browse nearby places by category, and show Apple Pay and landmark information on place cards.

changes.title: Redesigned Notes
changes.canonicalSummary: Notes gained photos, checklists, sketches, and share-sheet capture from other apps.
changes.summary: The redesigned Notes app supported camera and library images, tappable checklists, finger sketches, and saving material shared from other applications.

changes.title: Apple News app
changes.canonicalSummary: A new News app organized publications and topics into personalized, media-rich reading feeds with offline saving.
changes.summary: News launched with publication and topic discovery, personalized For You recommendations, media-rich article layouts, sharing, and offline reading.

changes.title: Mail search, Markup, and attachments
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail added combined search filters, attachment annotation, and document-provider integration.
changes.summary: Users could narrow Mail searches by message fields, annotate image and PDF attachments without leaving Mail, and attach or save files through iCloud Drive and compatible providers.

changes.title: Low Power Mode and platform efficiency
changes.canonicalSummary: The platform added Low Power Mode, reduced update download requirements, and used Metal for system-interface rendering.
changes.summary: iOS 9 added a power-saving mode, made software updates smaller and schedulable, and moved more app and interface rendering onto Metal for smoother interaction.

changes.title: Account and passcode security defaults
changes.canonicalSummary: The platform added two-factor authentication support and defaulted Touch ID devices to six-digit passcodes.
changes.summary: iOS 9 strengthened account and device access through two-factor authentication support and a six-digit default passcode on Touch ID hardware.

changes.title: Safari bookmark data protection
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari bookmarks on locked devices were protected with encryption tied to both the hardware and the user’s passcode.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-7118 by changing Safari bookmark encryption so a locked device’s bookmark data was not protected solely by the hardware identifier.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.0.1 release corrected Setup Assistant, alarm and timer playback, paused-video rendering, and custom-APN cellular data.

changes.title: Setup Assistant completion fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Affected devices could complete Setup Assistant after updating.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a condition that prevented some users from finishing Setup Assistant after the iOS 9 update.

changes.title: Alarm and timer audio fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Alarms and timers played their alert sound reliably.
changes.summary: The update addressed a failure that could leave alarms and timers silent.

changes.title: Paused video rendering fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Paused video frames no longer displayed the documented distortion in Safari and Photos.
changes.summary: Apple corrected distorted frames that could appear when pausing video in Safari or Photos.

changes.title: Custom APN cellular-data fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Profile-managed custom APN configurations retained cellular-data access.
changes.summary: The release restored cellular data for some users whose custom APN settings came from a configuration profile.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.0.2 release repaired cellular, activation, backup, rotation, and Podcasts behavior and closed a documented lock-screen data-access path.

changes.title: Per-app cellular-data setting fix
changes.canonicalSummary: The setting that controlled cellular use for individual apps retained its intended state.
changes.summary: Apple corrected the control used to turn cellular-data access on or off for individual applications.

changes.title: iMessage activation fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Affected users could activate iMessage.
changes.summary: The update resolved an activation failure affecting iMessage for some users.

changes.title: Manual iCloud Backup fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A manually started iCloud Backup could proceed without the documented interruption.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a condition that could interrupt an iCloud Backup after a user started it manually.

changes.title: Notification rotation fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Incoming notifications no longer caused the documented incorrect screen rotation.
changes.summary: The release addressed an orientation problem that could rotate the screen incorrectly when a notification arrived.

changes.title: Podcasts stability improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: The Podcasts app became more stable.
changes.summary: Apple’s release notes identify a general stability improvement for Podcasts without naming a narrower failure mode.

changes.title: Lock-screen photos and contacts restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: Restricted lock-screen options blocked the documented physical-access path to photos and contacts.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-5923 by limiting the options available from a locked device so the affected path could not expose photos and contacts.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.1 release refined Live Photos, added more than 150 emoji, improved stability and multitasking, repaired several apps and services, and delivered security fixes.

changes.title: Live Photos raise-and-lower detection
changes.canonicalSummary: Live Photos excluded movement caused by raising or lowering the iPhone from the captured moment.
changes.summary: The camera began recognizing when an iPhone was being raised or lowered so those motions were not recorded as part of a Live Photo.

changes.title: Unicode emoji expansion
changes.canonicalSummary: The emoji keyboard added more than 150 characters with Unicode 7.0 and 8.0 support.
changes.summary: iOS 9.1 expanded the available emoji set by more than 150 characters and added full support for the documented Unicode versions.

changes.title: App stability and multitasking performance
changes.canonicalSummary: CarPlay, Music, Photos, Safari, Search, and the multitasking interface received stability or performance improvements.
changes.summary: Apple grouped stability improvements for several system experiences with a separate performance improvement for the multitasking interface.

changes.title: Calendar, Game Center, and app display fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Calendar remained responsive in Month view, Game Center launched, and affected apps no longer displayed unintended zoom.
changes.summary: The update corrected a Calendar Month-view hang, a Game Center launch failure, and unexpected content zoom in some applications.

citations.locator: iOS 9.1 — Calendar, Game Center, and zoom

changes.title: Mail and Messages corrections
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail counts, recent-contact removal, search results, and Audio Message rendering worked as documented.
changes.summary: Apple corrected incorrect POP unread counts, recent-contact removal, absent Mail search results, and a gray bar that could appear inside an Audio Message.

citations.locator: iOS 9.1 — Mail and Audio Message fixes

changes.title: Carrier activation and App Store update fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Affected devices activated with their carrier and installed application updates from the App Store.
changes.summary: The maintenance pass addressed carrier activation errors and an issue that prevented some apps from updating through the App Store.

changes.title: Lock-screen notification privacy fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Phone and Messages respected changes that disabled their lock-screen notifications.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-7000 by applying Phone and Messages notification-setting changes immediately so disabled content did not continue appearing on the Lock Screen.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.2 release expanded media and reading workflows, added Mail Drop and camera-adapter support, repaired app, backup, and keyboard behavior, improved accessibility, and delivered security fixes.

changes.title: Apple Music library workflow improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Music added playlist creation while adding songs, recent-playlist ordering, album and playlist downloads, download indicators, and richer classical metadata.
changes.summary: The Music app streamlined playlist and offline-library management and displayed works, composers, and performers while browsing classical music.

changes.title: News Top Stories
changes.canonicalSummary: News added a Top Stories section in the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia.
changes.summary: The News app gained a Top Stories area highlighting major stories for readers in the three documented launch countries.

changes.title: Mail Drop and iBooks expansion
changes.canonicalSummary: Mail could send large attachments through Mail Drop, while iBooks added 3D Touch previews and background audiobook playback.
changes.summary: iOS 9.2 brought Mail Drop to the Mail app and let iBooks users preview book locations with 3D Touch or continue an audiobook while browsing elsewhere in the app.

changes.title: iPhone USB Camera Adapter support
changes.canonicalSummary: iPhone could import photos and videos through the USB Camera Adapter.
changes.summary: The release extended USB Camera Adapter photo and video importing to iPhone.

changes.title: App, data, backup, and alert reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: A grouped maintenance pass corrected app stability, missing data, Wallet alerts, alarms, account login, and manual backups.
changes.summary: Apple addressed Safari and Podcasts stability, missing Health data, absent Wallet updates, silent alarms after updating, Find My iPhone login failures, and incomplete manual iCloud Backups.

citations.locator: iOS 9.2 — stability, Health, Wallet, alarms, Find My iPhone, and backups

changes.title: Keyboard input reliability
changes.canonicalSummary: iPad selection, Quick Reply, Chinese punctuation, and Cyrillic capitalization behavior were corrected or improved.
changes.summary: The keyboard update reduced accidental iPad text selection, improved Quick Reply responsiveness and Chinese 10-key punctuation, and prevented unintended Cyrillic caps lock in URL and email fields.

changes.title: Accessibility improvements and Arabic Siri
changes.canonicalSummary: VoiceOver, Guided Access, Switch Control, and Speak Screen improved, and Siri added Arabic support for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
changes.summary: The release expanded VoiceOver gestures and screen wake behavior, repaired accessibility workflows, improved Switch Control with 3D Touch, and added Siri support for two Arabic locales.

changes.title: Revoked Contacts access enforcement
changes.canonicalSummary: App sandbox hardening prevented a malicious app from retaining Contacts access after permission was revoked.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2015-7001 by hardening the sandbox’s handling of hard links so revoked Contacts permission remained effective.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.2.1 release repaired MDM-managed app installation and delivered documented security corrections, including captive-portal cookie isolation.

changes.title: MDM app installation completion
changes.canonicalSummary: Applications deployed through an MDM server could complete installation.
changes.summary: Apple fixed a condition that could prevent an app installation managed by an MDM server from finishing.

changes.title: Captive-portal cookie isolation
changes.canonicalSummary: Captive portals used an isolated cookie store instead of accessing a user’s normal web cookies.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-1730 by isolating cookies for captive portals, preventing the documented read-or-write access to a user’s cookies.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.3 release introduced Night Shift, expanded core apps and education deployment, improved CarPlay and system services, repaired broad reliability issues, and delivered security fixes.

changes.title: Night Shift
changes.canonicalSummary: Night Shift could automatically warm the display colors after sunset using the device clock and location.
changes.summary: The new Night Shift setting used time and geolocation to shift supported displays toward warmer colors on an automatic sunset schedule.

changes.title: Protected and expanded Notes
changes.canonicalSummary: Notes added Touch ID or passcode protection, sorting, faster sketch and checklist tools, attachment display controls, media-storage choices, and Evernote export importing.
changes.summary: Users could lock sensitive notes and gained new organization, sketching, checklist, attachment, camera-media, and Evernote import workflows.

changes.title: News reading and discovery improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: News expanded Top Stories, editor-selected discovery, feed gestures, inline video, landscape reading, and text-size controls.
changes.summary: The News app made prominent and curated stories easier to find, added direct feed actions and video playback, and improved article viewing on iPhone.

changes.title: Health and Activity integration
changes.canonicalSummary: Health surfaced related apps and Apple Watch activity data, added Home-screen shortcuts, and exposed Activity summaries through HealthKit.
changes.summary: Health linked selected data types to compatible apps, incorporated Apple Watch goals, added 3D Touch access, and made Activity rings and summaries available to third-party apps through HealthKit.

changes.title: Apple Music refinements
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Music improved playlist additions, iPad music-video viewing, Beats 1 discovery, album navigation, and popularity indicators.
changes.summary: Subscribers could add catalog songs to playlists without first adding them to the library, use full-screen video on iPad, see live Beats 1 content, navigate to an album, and identify popular tracks.

changes.title: Photos and iBooks expansion
changes.canonicalSummary: Photos improved Live Photo and iCloud workflows, while iBooks added iCloud PDF storage, audiobook and Family Sharing support, manga controls, and Apple Pencil highlighting.
changes.summary: The release let users extract a still image from a Live Photo, improved original-media downloads and Live Photo sharing, and broadened iBooks synchronization, purchase, reading, and annotation tools.

changes.title: Shared iPad and Classroom support
changes.canonicalSummary: Education deployments gained a Shared iPad preview, Managed Apple ID sign-in, Classroom compatibility, Home Screen controls, and new service restrictions.
changes.summary: Schools could preview multi-student use of one iPad, sign in with managed identities, use the Classroom app, control Home Screen organization and visibility, and restrict selected iCloud and Music services.

changes.title: CarPlay Music, Maps, Siri, and audio improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: CarPlay expanded Apple Music discovery, added nearby driving categories, shortened Siri messaging responses, and balanced audio-source levels.
changes.summary: CarPlay added For You and New music areas, a Maps Nearby screen for driving essentials, more concise Siri messaging, and more consistent loudness between audio sources.

changes.title: Maps, Wallet, Apple Pay, Podcasts, and Activity updates
changes.canonicalSummary: System apps gained transit-line detail, card-linked app access, store rewards enrollment, full-screen podcast video, and monthly workout summaries.
changes.summary: Maps clarified transit routes, Wallet linked passes to their apps, Apple Pay supported in-store rewards enrollment, Podcasts played full-screen video, and Activity added a filterable Workout history.

changes.title: Enterprise, accessibility, and system reliability fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: A broad maintenance pass addressed managed apps, profiles, VPN, Exchange, VoiceOver, Switch Control, backups, activation, battery reporting, Phone, Mail, and other system behavior.
changes.summary: Apple documented repairs across enterprise deployment, accessibility, device startup after extreme date changes, iCloud Backup and restore, iMessage and FaceTime activation, call presentation, restrictions, Watch settings, 3D Touch, voicemail, and low-storage Mail.

citations.locator: iOS 9.3 — Enterprise, Accessibility, and Other bug fixes

changes.title: Messages attachment cryptography fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Clients rejected duplicate encrypted attachment messages to address the documented attachment-disclosure scenario.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-1788 by rejecting duplicate messages, correcting a cryptographic weakness in the narrowly described attack path against encrypted Messages attachments.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.3.1 release corrected application hangs caused by opening links and carried forward the security content of iOS 9.3.

citations.locator: iOS 9.3.1 includes the security content of iOS 9.3

changes.title: Link-opening application freeze fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Applications remained responsive after a user tapped links in Safari or other apps.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a condition in which opening a link from Safari or another application could make apps unresponsive.

citations.locator: iOS 9.3.1 — links in Safari and other apps

events.summary: The public iOS 9.3.2 release repaired Bluetooth, dictionary, keyboard, VoiceOver, and managed-app behavior and delivered additional security corrections.

changes.title: iPhone SE Bluetooth audio fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Bluetooth accessories paired with iPhone SE avoided the documented audio-quality problem.
changes.summary: Apple corrected degraded audio quality affecting some Bluetooth accessories when used with iPhone SE.

citations.locator: iOS 9.3.2 — Bluetooth accessories and iPhone SE

changes.title: Dictionary definition lookup fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Dictionary definition lookups completed successfully.
changes.summary: The update repaired a failure that could prevent the system from looking up a word’s dictionary definition.

changes.title: Japanese Kana email-address entry fix
changes.canonicalSummary: The Japanese Kana keyboard could enter email addresses in Mail and Messages.
changes.summary: Apple addressed a Japanese Kana keyboard issue that blocked email-address entry in Mail and Messages.

changes.title: VoiceOver Alex voice consistency
changes.canonicalSummary: VoiceOver kept the Alex voice when announcing punctuation and spaces.
changes.summary: The release prevented VoiceOver from unexpectedly switching away from the Alex voice for punctuation or spaces.

changes.title: MDM Custom B2B app installation fix
changes.canonicalSummary: MDM servers could install Custom B2B applications.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a deployment issue that prevented MDM servers from installing Custom B2B apps.

changes.title: Safari history deletion fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Clear History and Website Data fully removed the affected browsing history.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-1849 by improving Safari’s data deletion so the documented history could be fully cleared.

changes.title: Siri lock-screen data restriction
changes.canonicalSummary: Locked devices suppressed the affected data detectors in Siri results to protect contacts and photos.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-1852 by disabling data detectors in the relevant Siri result while locked, closing a physical-access path to contacts and photos.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.3.3 release was a general bug-fix and security update whose bulletin documents specific Calendar, networking, FaceTime, Siri, and WebKit corrections.

changes.title: Calendar invitation restart fix
changes.canonicalSummary: A maliciously crafted calendar invitation no longer caused the documented unexpected device restart.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4605 by improving memory handling around the affected Calendar invitation path.

changes.title: Stored HTTP authentication downgrade fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Keychain credentials retained their authentication type to prevent the documented downgrade and information leak.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4644 by storing the HTTP authentication type with saved credentials, preventing the affected downgrade behavior.

changes.title: Relayed FaceTime call state fix
changes.canonicalSummary: FaceTime display logic accurately reflected whether a relayed call was still transmitting audio.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4635 by improving FaceTime’s display logic so the affected relayed call did not appear ended while audio transmission continued.

changes.title: Siri private contact information fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved state management protected private contact-card information from physical access through Siri.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4593 by correcting Siri’s handling of contact cards in the documented physical-access scenario.

changes.title: WebKit cross-origin redirect fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved URL validation prevented the documented cross-origin data leak through Safari redirection.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4585 by validating redirected URLs more strictly in the affected WebKit page-loading path.

events.summary: The public iOS 9.3.5 release delivered three documented security corrections affecting kernel information disclosure, kernel code execution, and WebKit code execution.

changes.title: Kernel information-disclosure fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved input sanitization prevented an application from disclosing kernel memory through the documented path.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4655, a kernel validation issue that could expose kernel memory to an application.

changes.title: Kernel memory-corruption fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved memory handling closed a kernel corruption path that could allow an application to execute code with kernel privileges.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4656, a kernel memory-corruption vulnerability with the documented potential for privileged code execution.

changes.title: WebKit memory-corruption fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Improved memory handling prevented the documented code-execution path through malicious web content.
changes.summary: Apple addressed CVE-2016-4657, a WebKit memory-corruption vulnerability triggered by maliciously crafted web content.
